summary: @servicetitan/toolbelt-shared-registry preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727 KB bundle
details: The package advertises itself as a React shared-registry library (dist/index.js re-exports React registries; peerDependencies include react and @servicetitan/react-ioc), but its package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13), extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the shipped sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose top-level code is a shuffled string-array decoder (`function WV8StW(...) { for(...) MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift()); }`) rotating a ~1500-entry array of hex constants — obfuscator.io-style string-array plus rotation obfuscation with no plaintext URLs, module structure, or comments. A pure browser React library has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate runtime at install time or to execute an obfuscated compiled bundle. Installing this version causes the obfuscated payload to execute on the installer's host under a freshly downloaded Bun interpreter that Node-based tooling will not evaluate, matching the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern where the fetched-and-executed content is unrelated to and unnecessary for the package's stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
